statements.action_statement: No fixed release is available yet; update when Docker Hardened Images publishes one.
statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-84786 ("Possible NULL Dereference in Non-SMTP DANE Clients"): a DANE-enabled TLS client that accepts PKIX-TA(0) or PKIX-EE(1) TLSA records alongside DANE-TA(2) can dereference a NULL pointer and crash when a server presents a trusted CA certificate as its end-entity certificate with an unusual mix of TLSA records. The CVE record says DANE SMTP clients should not be affected, since SMTP uses only the DANE-TA(2) and DANE-EE(3) usages. The CVE record lists OpenSSL 3.5.0 up to but not including 3.5.10 as affected and places the DANE API outside the FIPS module boundary (https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-84786). The fix is proposed in https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/33634, which changes the DANE checks in crypto/x509/x509_vfy.c and is not merged; no OpenSSL release carries it. Debian lists trixie as vulnerable, including 3.5.9-1~deb13u1 (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-84786). Every published DHI Debian 13 openssl build (25 versions, amd64 and arm64, from the DHI Debian repository and the DHI security repository), including the FIPS builds, ships libcrypto and libssl from OpenSSL 3.5.5, 3.5.6, 3.5.7 or 3.5.9 (the version string in libcrypto.so.3) without a backport of this fix: the changelog shipped in libssl3t64 of every one of those builds has no entry for it, while the same check finds the entry for another backported OpenSSL fix (CVE-2026-35190) in the builds that carry it. Every build is affected. The openssl-provider-fips packages hold the FIPS provider module (fips.so) and its documentation; their fips.so is the OpenSSL 3.5.5, 3.5.6, 3.5.7 or 3.5.9 provider in the non-FIPS builds and the OpenSSL 3.1.2 provider in the FIPS builds. The DANE checks are built into libcrypto, not into the FIPS provider module.
